work_order.understanding: Issue #29 collects six non-blocking review findings from PR #27 (for #24) and asks each be re-checked before planning, and dropped if it does not hold up. Re-checked all six against the tree at 63633ad; they split three ways. Three are real code work: (2) the electron test restores its console.log spy and closes both better-sqlite3 handles as the last three statements of the test body (index.electron.test.ts:81-83), so a failing assertion above them skips both — confirmed, since packages/loot-core/src/mocks/setup.ts:161 runs afterEach but never vi.restoreAllMocks(); (3) the web test at index.test.ts:303 opens two sql.js handles and never closes them (grep for closeDatabase returns 0); (6) the web case repeats a six-line runQuery block three times where a local query(db, pattern) helper — the shape index.electron.test.ts:50-56 already uses — says it in one line. Three are not code changes: (1) #24's AC-4 named the wrong import mechanism, so the fix is to the criterion not the file; (4) a merged PR's title/body accuracy; (5) the repo-wide customConditions gap the reviewer explicitly ruled out of a test-only PR. The change is confined to the two sqlite test files.
work_order.root_cause: The two new tests written in PR #27 put their cleanup at the end of the test body rather than in an afterEach, so cleanup is skipped whenever an assertion above it fails. The web copy also inlined its query call three times instead of using the local helper its electron twin already has. Neither is a product-code defect: the REGEXP dedupe fix in index.electron.ts:130 and index.ts:220 is correct. Test hygiene only.
work_order.approach: Two test files, no product code. In index.electron.test.ts, hoist teardown into a describe-level afterEach (vi.restoreAllMocks plus closing every handle in a describe-scoped `handles` array), matching ../connection/index.api.test.ts:4-6, and delete the trailing three statements at lines 81-83. Make the fix falsifiable — this is where v1 was wrong. v1 proposed an `it.fails` guard alone and named 'expected true to be false' as its message; that guard could never emit it, because it.fails passes whether or not the afterEach exists and nothing downstream observed the leak. The corrected mechanism has two coordinated halves, both required: (1) keep the `it.fails` guard first — spy on console.log, open a handle, push it onto `handles`, assert something deliberately false; (2) add `expect(vi.isMockFunction(console.log)).toBe(false)` as the FIRST statement of the existing test, before its own vi.spyOn at line 42. I ran both directions in a scratch vitest 5.0.3 harness: with the afterEach, '1 passed | 1 expected fail', exit 0; with the block deleted, the following test fails 'expected true to be false'. The failure surfaces in the FOLLOWING test, never in the it.fails test, so AC-1/AC-2 say exactly that. In index.test.ts, add a local query(db, pattern) helper passing null — matching the three replaced calls verbatim, so assertions are unchanged — and close both handles with closeDatabase, already exported at index.ts:289. v1 had the backend asymmetry backwards and the review caught it: web binds (index.ts:114), electron spreads (index.electron.ts:60,66); [] is what the ELECTRON backend requires, so no 'params is not iterable' probe is claimed on web.

files.change: Add a describe-scoped `const handles: Database[] = []` and a describe-level `afterEach(() => { vi.restoreAllMocks(); for (const handle of handles.splice(0)) { handle.close(); } })` as the first statements inside `describe('Native sqlite REGEXP guard', ...)`, matching ../connection/index.api.test.ts:4-6. Add an `it.fails(...)` as the FIRST test: it spies on console.log, opens a handle, pushes it onto `handles`, runs execQuery, then asserts `expect('never called').toBe('called')`. SECOND, add `expect(vi.isMockFunction(console.log)).toBe(false);` as the very first statement of the existing test, BEFORE its own `vi.spyOn` at line 42 — this is what makes the guard load-bearing. Push db1/db2 onto `handles` after each openDatabase call and delete the trailing mockRestore/close at lines 81-83. All globals (afterEach, it.fails, vi) come from vitest globals:true, so add no import.

The repo has no precedent, and the guard is now only half the proof (the other half being the following test's isMockFunction assertion). A reviewer who rejects it.fails should reject only the guard; the afterEach and the assertion stand on their own.

Whether closing only two of the nine handles in index.test.ts reads as an arbitrary line in the diff or as correct scoping. I judged it scoping — the ticket is the two tests PR #27 added — but a reviewer may reasonably ask for all of them.
residual_risks: The web test file now closes handles in one case and not in eight others. A future reader may reasonably ask why; the diff should make the scoping obvious rather than looking like an oversight.

The isMockFunction assertion is position-sensitive — only meaningful before the test's own spy. A later edit that moves it below line 42 would make AC-1 unsatisfiable-by-accident rather than catch the regression, which is why the qa_script checks the position explicitly.

If it.fails is rejected at review, the afterEach and the isMockFunction assertion still stand on their own — but the ticket's falsifiability claim weakens, and the leak would only be caught by the next person who happens to break an assertion in that file.
